races.name: Personal Touches Day Of Elegance Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Empire Rising
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field, Darragh Keenan takes the ride for Charlie Clover whose T14 reads a modest 1/3; steps up to a mile after a sequence of sixth-furlong runs and his sole win came over 8f on good ground — the trip suits but soft ground is an unknown quantity, and any capitulation late would be sudden given the pace role he must fulfil.

runners_data.name: Love Tanya
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this Edward Bethell runner who has been remarkably consistent with two seconds from three starts over seven furlongs on good ground; the step up to a mile is the key question but her hold-up style and stamina-biased form suggest the extra furlong on soft ground could play to her strengths, and Bethell's yard is in solid form.

runners_data.name: The Monkey King
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's colt arrives as the most recent winner in the field, landing a seven-furlong contest on good ground 30 days ago, and steps up to a mile in first-time handicap company; Rhys Clutterbuck retains the ride and a prominent racing style means he will be ideally placed to strike if Empire Rising's lead is catchable in the straight.

runners_data.name: Coco Nova
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly is lightly raced with just two runs — both on good ground over seven and eight furlongs — which gives the form assessor very little to work with; Harry Davies takes the ride and, with an unclassified style, she is a genuine unknown quantity who could slot anywhere from midfield to prominent, making her a dark horse if the form step up matches her ability.

runners_data.name: Akaraka
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's hold-up runner has three runs in a row finishing seventh, eighth, and seventh on good ground over six and seven furlongs, which makes it hard to construct a winning argument at present; Pierre-Louis Jamin rides and the step up to a mile on soft ground could unlock improvement, but the form is discouraging and there is little pace evidence to back a dramatic turnaround.

runners_data.name: Or Another
runners_data.note: Showed his best form finishing third over five and six furlongs on good ground, and Jason Hart rides for Katie Scott whose T14 returns zero wins from ten; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural rear position is compromised in this field by the volume of similar types, meaning he is likely to race in midfield rather than off a true back-of-the-field position — a slight style mismatch that tempers his chance.

runners_data.name: Prince Kameo
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's runner won over eight furlongs at Salisbury on standard going nine days ago, making him the freshest recent winner in the field; Kevin Stott partners and the seven-day turnaround is typical of Prescott's operation, but his similar-going record shows zero wins from five on comparable surfaces and he remains a watch-with-interest rather than a confident selection.

runners_data.name: Sou'wester
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up type has run five-five-five in three races, including once over seven furlongs on soft ground, and returns after an 86-day break with David Allan aboard; his natural inclination to race from the rear is squeezed in a field this strong on hold-up types, pushing him towards midfield in practice, and a long absence combined with that consistent mid-table placing does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Northern Viola
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's filly has form figures of seven-five-five over five and seven furlongs on good ground, all on good going, and has not run for 64 days; James Sullivan rides and, while she drops significantly in weight on OR 55, the pattern of finishes and the fact that soft ground is unexplored territory make it difficult to see a route to the frame even if she finds a more prominent position than her natural style suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Empire Rising is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will be able to dictate from the front at whatever tempo suits Charlie Clover's instructions on Good to Soft ground over a mile. The hold-up brigade is crowded — Love Tanya, Akaraka, Prince Kameo, Or Another, Sou'wester, and Northern Viola all want to race from the rear, but with so many true hold-up types in the field, not all will secure their preferred position; Or Another, Sou'wester, and Northern Viola have been redistributed to the midfield map-position as genuine hold-up horses unlikely to get buried at the back in this particular shape. The Monkey King will press forward into a prominent position behind the leader, giving Empire Rising a shadow but not a serious fight for the front, while Coco Nova's unknown tactical profile adds a small wildcard element. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner controlling a sustainable gallop on soft ground over a mile — decisively favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles who can track the pace and unleash a sustained run through the final two furlongs, rather than those who must come from the very back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Empire Rising Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Empire Rising dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Empire Rising, untroubled from the front, sets a measured pace that softens the field without burning himself out, and his recent form line of four finishes at the track combined with a winning run over 8f on good ground suggests he can see out the mile at this level; the soft ground may slow closers enough that his lead proves insurmountable in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Empire Rising sets an honest enough gallop that The Monkey King or Coco Nova, tracking just off the pace, have enough energy to collar him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The Monkey King arrives at Thirsk on the back of a seven-furlong win on good ground, is stepping up to a mile for the first time, and Ralph Beckett's record with improvers at this trip gives the step-up strong credentials; tracking the front-runner throughout and kicking from two out suits a prominent racer on soft ground where acceleration is limited and relentless grinding wins.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Empire Rising sets a genuinely strong pace that burns off the prominent horses, leaving the race wide open for hold-up runners in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Love Tanya, who has run two consecutive seconds over seven furlongs on good ground, steps up to a mile for the first time and Edward Bethell's 3/27 fourteen-day record suggests in-form runners from his yard; a strong pace from the front would suit a staying hold-up type finding extra on the mile trip, and Connor Beasley's positional awareness is a significant asset.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground takes a severe toll, Empire Rising fades quickly, and the race becomes a rough-and-tumble sprint for the line from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: In a scenario where no horse has a true tactical advantage due to a collapsed pace, lower-rated horses with stamina reserves could outrun their odds, but Or Another, Sou'wester, and Northern Viola — true hold-up types forced into midfield — are racing somewhat out of their natural role in this shape and their style-fit discount tempers expectation significantly.

watchPoints.text: Empire Rising — the lone front-runner will set the race shape entirely; watch whether Darragh Keenan elects to bowl along or conserve early, as any significant change of pace at the two-furlong marker will determine whether this race is for passers or holders.

The Monkey King — if Rhys Clutterbuck is able to track Empire Rising just a length or two off the pace through the early furlongs, he is in the ideal position to challenge in the straight and a strong closing move would not be a surprise given the step up in trip.

Love Tanya — Connor Beasley's mount is consistent without winning and the mile trip is uncharted; watch the betting market closely as any market support would suggest connections are confident the extra furlong on soft ground is the key upgrade her form has been waiting for.

Prince Kameo — only nine days since his last run and Prescott's rapid-turnaround runners often improve markedly; the soft ground is a question mark based on his sim-going record, but he should not be dismissed purely on pace-position grounds given his recent winning form over the mile trip.

Sou'wester — an 86-day absence for Tim Easterby, a handler who can place freshened horses to good effect; if this runner comes on significantly for the run from a forward position rather than his natural rear station, a better showing than his three recent fifths would not be unprecedented from this stable.

races.name: Jw4x4 Northallerton Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Roots In Touche
runners_data.note: Trainer Keatley blank in 14 days (0/12) and wearing a hood; a genuine front-runner who led and placed on good ground but finished eighth latest on soft, and with a contested pace rival in Black Velvet Boy, clean air off the front is not guaranteed.|

runners_data.name: Casino Star
runners_data.note: Burke's operation runs at 8/41 in the 14-day window and Pierre-Louis Jamin has strong course form; a natural hold-up horse who placed on soft at six furlongs last time, meaning today's conditions and a hot pace should suit his late style well.|

runners_data.name: Concert Pitch
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison returns a modest 1/21 recently, but this filly has been relentlessly consistent with three placed efforts and a win at five furlongs on similar ground, and settling off a frantic early pace as a prominent type could gift her a well-timed run.|

runners_data.name: This Moment
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 83 alongside three rivals and represents George Boughey (1/25 in 14 days); naturally prominent, she won at this trip on Standard going and has placed five times from six starts, but traffic danger in a crowded vanguard is a real tactical risk.|

runners_data.name: Black Velvet Boy
runners_data.note: Quinn yard in fair recent form (3/17); won back-to-back on good ground at this course and trip and possesses genuine pace, but has never raced on soft and faces a direct rival in Roots In Touche who will contest every metre of the early lead.|

runners_data.name: Furturra
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby, who runs an active yard (10/83), sends this filly back nine days after a poor run on soft at Beverley (13th of 13); her best form came on good-to-good-firm over six furlongs and the combination of soft ground and a compressed five furlongs is a live concern.|

runners_data.name: Princesse d'Orange
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's yard is active (7/50) and Kevin Stott takes the ride; she is the only runner with a soft-ground win to her name, a maiden score at five furlongs in that exact condition, and 38 days off adds a small fitness question, though O'Meara regularly returns horses fresh.|

runners_data.name: Savage Mariner
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer sends this colt with a clear flag — he fades in the finish — and his form reads 2000 with his three recent runs yielding finishes of 16th, 11th and 19th; the hold-up style combined with the stamina flag makes this a very difficult puzzle on soft ground.|

runners_data.name: Anchiano
runners_data.note: George Scott's gelding hasn't run for 44 days and wears a hood; he won over this course and trip on good ground and then finished third next time, but there are no soft-ground runs in his history, meaning going suitability is a genuine unknown despite the eye-catching trainer angle.|

races.paceDynamic: Black Velvet Boy and Roots In Touche are the confirmed pace-setters, and with four of nine runners wanting a prominent position, the opening furlong on this Good To Soft Thirsk five will be genuinely contested rather than a procession. Concert Pitch, This Moment, Furturra, and Princesse d'Orange all want to be in the first three or four, meaning traffic pinch-points are virtually certain between the two-furlong and three-furlong pole as they jostle for slots. The two leaders will ensure an honest, possibly pressured gallop that burns energy quickly on a soft surface, and any front-runner who is harried rather than allowed to stride free will be vulnerable late. This race shape firmly favours a closer or a horse who can settle just off the friction zone and pick up the pieces — a genuine hold-up or late-prominent runner who saves their energy through the scramble is the profile to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Black Velvet Boy and Roots In Touche fight for the lead and burn each other out on the soft, allowing off-pace runners to swoop.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop set by two genuine front-runners drains their reserves on testing ground, leaving the final furlong open for horses who have been patient; Casino Star and Anchiano, both natural hold-up types, are ideally placed to exploit spent leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Black Velvet Boy repels Roots In Touche early and secures a clear lead without sustained pressure, dictating an even gallop.
scenarios.body: Black Velvet Boy's back-to-back course wins on good ground suggest tactical speed in reserve, and if he escapes clean he can husband his effort and hold on as the prominent cluster gets bunched behind him; on the softer surface the question is stamina, which his recent course form suggests he handles adequately.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Surge Wins It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but even and a prominent-travelling runner settles just behind the leaders and picks off the weakening front pair.
scenarios.body: Concert Pitch's consistent placed form at five furlongs, including a win and multiple seconds at this trip on similar ground, makes her the likeliest beneficiary of this shape; This Moment, who scored at this trip and has placed repeatedly over six, has the tactical position to land a blow if she travels sweetly through the congestion.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Soft Ground Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage causes interference two-to-three out and the race turns into a stamina test on heavy-ish ground, with no clean run available until late.
scenarios.body: Princesse d'Orange's sole soft-ground win and Anchiano's prior course win give them each a pedigree for this scenario, but Savage Mariner's flagged tendency to fade in the finish makes this shape the most dangerous for him; the chaotic traffic scenario is the least predictable outcome but genuinely possible given the four-runner prominent cluster.

watchPoints.text: Black Velvet Boy and Roots In Touche — watch the first two furlongs for direct front-running conflict; whichever is pressured into sprinting rather than striding will likely exhaust itself before the final furlong on this soft surface.

The four-runner prominent cluster (Concert Pitch, This Moment, Furturra, Princesse d'Orange) creates a serious traffic risk between the two and three furlong marks — any runner squeezed or forced to check at that point effectively loses the race.
Furturra's very quick turnaround (9 days) after a catastrophic soft-ground run (13th of 13 at Beverley) is a significant red flag — watch for her to be outpaced early if the pace becomes intense.

Savage Mariner's flagged tendency to fade in the finish combined with his string of poor recent form (16th, 11th, 19th) means he is a horse to watch drifting backwards through the field from the two-furlong pole, which could create passage problems for closers behind him.

Anchiano's 44-day absence and first run in soft conditions is worth monitoring in the market — any significant drift in price may reflect stable intelligence about readiness, whereas support would upgrade his each-way claims considerably.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ma Blushin Rosie
runners_data.note: Ran third on soft ground over 6f on her only start, giving her the most directly relevant form in this field; Adrian Keatley sends her across from Ireland 17 days fresh and she is clearly suited to these conditions racing prominently.

runners_data.name: Scottys Rocket
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's filly has run twice on good ground at 5f, finishing third and ninth, so both the step up to 6f and the softer conditions here are unknowns, though Joanna Mason's booking suggests connections are confident about the ground.

runners_data.name: Texting
runners_data.note: Has form at both 6f and 7f and shaped with ability on good, so the extra give underfoot is likely welcome for this hold-up type, though Ivan Furtado's 0-from-17 recent run rate warrants realistic expectations.

runners_data.name: Voyager One
runners_data.note: Ran fifth over 1m on good ground last time out for Michael Bell, whose string is in reasonable form (3 from 16 in 14 days); a hold-up horse stepping back in trip, the softer ground should help but the race shape here does not perfectly suit late runners.

runners_data.name: Malulee
runners_data.note: Has a warning flag for fading in the finish and her only run was an 11th at 5f on good, so the step to 6f on softer ground is unproven and Michael Dods' recent form figures (3 from 30) give little confidence about a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Uncle Zello
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's gelding is the race's confirmed front-runner and will likely get an uncontested lead, though his style-fit score of 0.93 flags he is racing slightly out of his best role today; his last run at 7f on Standard and a previous third at 6f on good suggests he handles varying conditions.

runners_data.name: Lord Bishop
runners_data.note: A debutant for Brian Ellison whose stable sends out a second runner in this race, adding stable confidence as context; going and style entirely unknown, though Ellison does win with lightly raced juveniles when he sends them out fresh.

runners_data.name: Callisterra
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' filly has a solid novice profile with a second and a third at 6f on good ground, and Connor Beasley's booking is a stable-jockey positive; she races prominently and the trip and conditions are within her comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Hair Raising
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's juvenile finished third at 5f and sixth at 8f, showing ability, but as a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position by the race shape, the tactical dynamics here do not align with how he runs best; style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Dontlookanyfurther
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground 14 days ago and is the most experienced and highest-weighted runner here at 134lbs, suggesting connections and handicapper both view him highly; Jason Hart's booking adds confidence and prominent racing style is well-suited to this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Pippy Boy
runners_data.note: A debutant for Jennie Candlish whose recent 1-from-9 yard form is modest; nothing known about style or ability, making him a complete unknown in terms of tactical fit but not without an outside chance if well-schooled.

runners_data.name: Rum Point
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's debut runner with zero form to assess; the trainer has sent out 2 winners from 9 runners in the last 14 days, showing the yard is not cold, but this horse is impossible to place tactically without evidence.

runners_data.name: Reddy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's only runner has one run to her name, a third at 6f on Standard at Southwell; the going switch to soft turf is uncharted territory but the trip is familiar, and the stable is in decent recent form (4 from 33).

races.paceDynamic: Uncle Zello is the one confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press him hard from the gates, he is expected to dictate a measured, controlled tempo on Good to Soft ground over 6f at Thirsk. Ma Blushin Rosie, Callisterra, and Dontlookanyfurther will look to sit prominently just off his shoulder, creating a compact lead group rather than a truly contested pace scenario. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can simultaneously occupy their natural positions, and with Hair Raising redistributed to midfield on the map — despite being a genuine hold-up horse — the race shape is unlikely to stretch out into a true end-to-end gallop. This setup, a sustainable if not dawdling pace, heavily favours horses who can travel prominently, conserve energy in the early stages, and produce a sustained finish through the final two furlongs rather than those relying on a strong pace collapse to deliver a late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Uncle Zello sets a measured pace and the prominent horses track comfortably before kicking clear in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Uncle Zello's controlled front-running creates a pace that suits those travelling just behind him, and horses like Ma Blushin Rosie and Callisterra, both with positive recent form at this trip on similar ground, are ideally positioned to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Uncle Zello finds a particularly comfortable rhythm and the field fails to close through soft ground late.
scenarios.body: On Good to Soft ground, a horse allowed to bowl along without pressure can find reserves that a pursuing pack drains trying to close, and Uncle Zello's 6f run on Good gives him a plausible stamina profile for this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally too hot early and frontrunners tie up, allowing a tracking horse to pick through.
scenarios.body: Hair Raising, though a true hold-up type placed in midfield here by race shape, could benefit if the pace proves deceptively strong and the front group come back to the field; Scottys Rocket from further back also has the form to capitalise on a strong pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Upset
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced unknown-style runners — Lord Bishop, Pippy Boy, or Rum Point — is significantly above average and debuts with a tactical advantage no form figure can quantify.
scenarios.body: A 6f novice on soft ground can sometimes be overturned by a well-prepared debutant with natural pace, and any of these three unknown quantities could hold a rating well above their current mark.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Uncle Zello is pressured out of the gates by Ma Blushin Rosie or Callisterra — if he is forced to quicken early on soft ground, his ability to sustain the lead into the final furlong drops sharply.

Dontlookanyfurther carries the heaviest weight in the field at 134lbs and won over this course and trip 14 days ago; any sign of freshness or ease in the ground suiting him could make him the most dangerous prominent horse in the race.

Hair Raising's true hold-up profile means he needs a stronger pace than this race shape is likely to generate — if the tempo is genuinely steady, his chance diminishes further beyond what the style-fit flag already implies.

Three debutants — Lord Bishop, Pippy Boy, and Rum Point — represent a combined unknown in a 13-runner field; if any arrives having worked with exceptional ability at home, the form book runners have limited protection against an unknown ceiling.

The going is officially Good to Soft rather than Soft as listed in the race header — this subtlety matters for horses like Scottys Rocket and Voyager One who have only run on good, as conditions may not be as testing as their connections anticipated.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Oolong Poobong
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed leader stepping back to 7f at Thirsk; sole soft-ground win came over this trip and the unchallenged role suits perfectly, though her style-fit tag reflects she holds prominent rather than true lead tendencies and her recent form string of 14-503 is mixed.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with soft-ground experience (two placings from 11 starts in cut), trained by Katie Scott whose 14-day record is quiet at 0/10; needs either a stronger pace or a stamina-test to make her finishing effort count from the rear.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose best recent effort was a 2nd over 8f on good ground; she has no wins from 15 soft/similar-going runs though she has placed four times, and Joanna Mason's patient ride will depend heavily on how much the pace tests the leaders.

runners_data.name: Passing Thought
runners_data.note: The most compelling prominent profile in the field — two wins on soft and good-to-soft ground, a 7f course win on good, and trainer Ed Walker firing in good form at 7/40 over 14 days; Ashley Lewis claims 3lb and Passing Thought should sit comfortably behind the leader in a controlled gallop.

runners_data.name: Cotai Belle
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has finished second in six of her last seven starts, her natural instinct is to race prominently but she is mapped to midfield here because the forward berths are already taken by Oolong Poobong and Passing Thought; the style displacement is her biggest tactical hurdle.

runners_data.name: Proposal
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained filly with a win over 7f and a placed run at Southwell, naturally prominent in style but unable to secure that position in this field configuration; 39 days off and racing in a role that doesn't match her best form make this a tricky assignment despite the strong yard.

races.paceDynamic: Oolong Poobong is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, she is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Soft ground over seven furlongs at Thirsk. Passing Thought is the only other confirmed prominent runner likely to secure a forward berth, tracking Oolong Poobong just off the pace and posing the most direct threat in a race where the lead is uncontested. Cotai Belle and Proposal are both natural front-runners by style but are mapped to midfield here because the race cannot accommodate three prominent horses all getting their preferred position — Oolong Poobong and Passing Thought are the pair most likely to actually dictate early. With a lone, unchallenged leader setting a measured tempo on soft ground, this race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent to midfield runners who can track close to the gallop and produce a sustained finish — true hold-up horses who need a fast, truly-run pace to make up ground late are at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Oolong Dictates, Proximity Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Oolong Poobong leads unchallenged and the pace remains controlled, horses racing close to the action throughout are best placed.
scenarios.body: Oolong Poobong controls the tempo from flag to finish on soft ground, meaning the race is run to suit those sitting just behind her rather than those held up in rear. Passing Thought, ideally positioned to track and pounce, and Cotai Belle — if she recovers any proximity despite redistribution — are the profile that benefits from a race run at a manageable, non-gruelling gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Oolong Poobong's early lead is faster than it appears and the ground extracts a toll, causing a late fade that allows hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Soft ground can expose front-runners who have led unchallenged but burned slightly more energy than the bare tempo suggests, opening the door for hold-up horses finishing strongly late. Figjam and Perfect Part, both genuine hold-up types with soft-ground form, are the profile to benefit if the race turns truly stamina-based in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Cotai Belle and Proposal push forward from their redistributed midfield positions, creating unexpected early pressure on Oolong Poobong.
scenarios.body: A more contested early pace than anticipated would compress the field and make the race more genuinely run, potentially suiting hold-up closers who get a stronger gallop to aim at. However, given both Cotai Belle and Proposal are racing out of their natural role, this scenario depends on circumstance rather than design and is structurally less reliable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition Test
scenarios.trigger: If conditions are significantly more testing than Good to Soft and the race becomes a thorough stamina examination, rewarding those with proven soft-ground credentials.
scenarios.body: A truly attritional seven furlongs on heavy-end ground would expose those without genuine soft-ground form and reward horses who have shown they handle cut efficiently. Passing Thought's two soft-ground wins and Perfect Part's consistent soft-ground placing give them the strongest profiles in this specific shape.

watchPoints.text: Passing Thought is the primary danger — two soft-ground wins, strong trainer form, and the only confirmed prominent runner positioned to track Oolong Poobong throughout; if the pace stays honest she gets every chance to pounce.

Monitor Cotai Belle's early behaviour — if she pushes forward aggressively from her redistributed midfield slot she could inadvertently create a more contested pace than the race map suggests, changing the shape materially.

Figjam's hold-up profile is entirely dependent on the gallop being genuinely strong enough to bring her into it; with a controlled front-runner and small field of six, Jason Hart may find himself too far back with nowhere to aim.

Oolong Poobong's recent form (14-503) includes a win on soft over 7f but also some flat efforts — watch in-running whether Connor Beasley tries to dictate or allows a more restrained lead, as the margin of control will shape the entire race.

Perfect Part has zero wins from 15 soft or similar-going starts despite four placings; her consistency is admirable but the absence of a win in this ground profile is a factual flag worth holding against her in a race where stamina is already premium.

races.name: Rudding Park Harrogate Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Musical Touch
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile for Richard Fahey; sim-going record at soft is poor (0W0P, one finish of 15th), 42-day break is notable, and Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim is the primary positive — needs a pace collapse to get involved.

runners_data.name: Grasmere Boy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer for Julie Camacho and Jason Hart; excellent recent form (two wins and two seconds in last four) on good ground, but all those runs came on good — soft is an untested query at this stage of his career.

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old has won twice at 6f on good recently, but she is a natural prominent type who will struggle to secure that position given the four rivals ahead of her for those slots; her STYLE_FIT flag is real — her chance is partly contingent on a fortuitous split.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby veteran with headgear; a genuine hold-up horse by inclination whose best soft-going form (2/15, 0W0P) gives little encouragement, and at OR 79 he is the lowest-rated runner — his midfield placement on the map reflects field density, not a change of tactics.

runners_data.name: Midnight Thunder
runners_data.note: Saeed bin Suroor's four-year-old carries top weight (137lbs) and wears a tongue-tie; his sole win came on good at 6f and his one comparable soft run produced a ninth — Pierre-Louis Jamin needs to secure a clean prominent pitch early.

runners_data.name: Commanche Falls
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old Michael Dods sprinter who is genuine and consistent at 6f; wears a hood (p), sim-going form is 0W0P from three runs, and recent form figures include zeroes — age and soft ground combine to make his chance conditional on a truly honest pace.

runners_data.name: Dapper Valley
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up type (back-to-back wins at 5f and 6f) with visor; Michael Keady's five-year-old is unexposed at 6f on soft, but his recent course-and-distance confidence is the most compelling form angle in the hold-up division — needs the pace to be genuine.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner (OR 97) but drops from 7-8f trips to 6f here, and all five recorded runs are on good ground — soft at a shorter trip is a significant double query for Adrian Keatley's horse and M. P. Sheehy.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old wears a visor (v) and is prominent in style; his sim-going record (1/15, 0W0P) is sparse but his recent form includes a win and a second at 6f on good — Billy Garritty must secure a clean pitch in the early scramble.

runners_data.name: Ray Mon Dough
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner for Oliver Cole and Kevin Stott; at OR 94 he is well-rated for the lead role, has a win and a second over this C&D trip, and an uncontested early lead on good-to-soft suits his profile ideally — the question is whether his stamina holds on this going.

races.paceDynamic: Ray Mon Dough is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge him, Kevin Stott should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on good-to-soft ground. Behind him, Grasmere Boy, Midnight Thunder, Commanche Falls, and Dark Cloud Rising all want prominent positions, creating a congested battle for the two or three berths immediately off the leader between the 3f and 2f poles — that scrimmage is the race's primary danger zone for traffic trouble. The field contains more genuine prominent/pace types than the map can accommodate: The Good Biscuit is a natural prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that spot given the competition ahead of her, and Fivethousandtoone, though a true hold-up type, is shown in midfield purely because of field density. With a single uncontested front-runner setting a measured, honest-but-not-brutal pace on soft ground over 6f, this race shape strongly favours horses who can sit handy in second or third without burning energy in the early scrimmage — prominent types with tactical speed and soft-ground stamina are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Ray Mon Dough dictates an uncontested, metronomic pace and the prominent pack fails to reel him in over the soft 6f.
scenarios.body: Ray Mon Dough sets a comfortable rhythm that is never truly pressured, and the energy expended by the prominent pack jostling for second position leaves them short of the finish; horses who settled cleanly in second or third without fighting for position hit the line strongest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent horses aggressively contest positions and force a genuine pace battle from the 2f pole, leaving the lead vulnerable.
scenarios.body: The early scrimmage burns Ray Mon Dough up faster than he can sustain, and a horse who grabbed a clean second or third slot without incident picks up the pieces; soft ground amplifies fatigue at the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the final furlong due to soft-ground attrition and all prominent horses tie up simultaneously.
scenarios.body: A hold-up horse who has tracked wide of trouble gets a clean run at the leaders as they flatten out; Musical Touch or Dapper Valley, both with finishing kicks on turf, could swoop late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Intervenes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion at the 2-3f mark causes interference that forces wide moves or checks, reshuffling the entire order violently.
scenarios.body: Horses drawn widest or tracking furthest back avoid the pocket and inherit clear daylight while the bunched mid-division finds its path repeatedly blocked; this is a minority scenario but the 10-runner field over 6f on soft increases its plausibility marginally.

watchPoints.text: Ray Mon Dough (lead) and the four prominent types — Grasmere Boy, Midnight Thunder, Commanche Falls, Dark Cloud Rising — will jostle aggressively for berths from the 3f to 2f mark; watch for checking, bumping and forced wide moves in that zone.

Mostar Dreams drops sharply in trip (from 7-8f to 6f) and has no soft-ground form — if she is outpaced early and settles too far back, M. P. Sheehy faces an impossible task on this ground at this distance.

The Good Biscuit's natural prominent style is squeezed out by four rivals ahead of her for those positions — if Joanna Mason tries to force the issue and secure it anyway, she risks burning the filly's finishing effort entirely.

Going is confirmed good-to-soft throughout the card, not soft as declared in the race conditions — the difference is meaningful for horses whose sim-going form is specifically at soft, and Ray Mon Dough's untested soft-ground stamina over 6f is the key late-race variable.

Fivethousandtoone (hg: p, hood) is an eight-year-old at the bottom of the weights — David Allan may drop him out to find cover, but his genuine hold-up profile means he needs the pace to be truly collapse-worthy to feature, which a controlled Ray Mon Dough lead makes less likely.

races.name: Calverts Carpets Hambleton Cup Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Acklam
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up mare whose best recent run was a win at 13f on good ground; soft going is not a concern based on her history, but a form figure of 9 last time out over this trip on soft is hard to dismiss, and with Joanna Mason aboard she will be ridden to get home late — a shape that needs a truly honest gallop to suit her.

runners_data.name: High Storm
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old has winning form on soft over 10f and is the lone confirmed pace-setter here, giving Pierre-Louis Jamin a golden opportunity to control the race from the front; 99 days off the track is a flag worth noting, but Burke's yard is in fine form at 8/41 over 14 days and the horse has shown it handles cut in the ground.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Myths
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old who won on a standard surface and placed on good ground, stepping up in trip significantly from 10f to 1m4f for Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole's yard, which has had no winners in the past 14 days from 13 runners; Ashley Lewis takes the 3lb claim, which helps offset the inexperience angle, and a prominent racing style suits this shape well if the stamina holds.

runners_data.name: What's The Plan
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's three-year-old has been remarkably consistent — five placed efforts in the last five runs, all over 10f on good ground — and steps up in trip and into soft going for the first time, which is the key question mark; Harry Davies rides, and the hold-up tag belies a horse that runs prominently enough to potentially track the pace here.

runners_data.name: Kisiyra
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent type whose form figures of 55/4-7 show limited improvement and no wins from nine runs on similar going, with the headgear flag and a 93-day absence adding further uncertainty; David Thompson's stable has just 1 winner from 9 runners in the past fortnight, and while the racing style suits this race shape, the evidence of ability is thin.

runners_data.name: Wardlaw
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old has back-to-back placed efforts at 12-14f on good ground and a win at 12f, making the trip and trainer angle genuinely compelling — but this is a true closer whose natural position at the rear of the field is compromised here, where the majority of the field also wants to come from off the pace; Kevin Stott will have to be creative if the pace doesn't materialise.

runners_data.name: Knightsail
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's three-year-old has run four times, all on good ground and mostly at 10f, and this is a step up to 1m4f on soft — two untested variables arriving together; Jason Hart partners a horse whose instinct is to race held up, which is a style that faces the same crowding problem as the other natural closers in this field, and the historical soft-going sample of just one run (7th) offers little confidence.

runners_data.name: Mr Bollinger
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old has winning form at 12f on good ground and placed form at the same trip, making the step to 1m4f credible — but soft ground is flagged as a concern given an 8th-place finish on soft over 8f last time; James Sullivan rides a horse who wants to finish late from off the pace, a profile that is working against the expected race shape today.

races.paceDynamic: High Storm is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 1m4f handicap on Good to Soft ground at Thirsk, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Pierre-Louis Jamin can dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front — a sustainable pace that will not burn off the field but will allow High Storm to conserve energy for a prolonged effort into the straight. Bay Of Myths and Kisiyra are the next most prominent types and will likely settle just behind, but neither has the profile or precedent to push High Storm off a comfortable lead, meaning the tempo is firmly in the front-runner's hands. The field is stacked with natural hold-up horses — Wardlaw, Knightsail, and Mr Bollinger are all true closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is no room at the rear, and their real tactical position will be further back than it appears, stretching the race into a long, strung-out shape. A steady, controlled pace over 1m4f on soft ground strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort, rather than closers who need a truly searching gallop to get into the race — the prominent-to-midfield profile is the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: High Storm Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If High Storm dictates a comfortable tempo throughout and the true closers cannot generate sufficient late momentum on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: High Storm sets a measured gallop with no meaningful pressure from Bay Of Myths or Kisiyra, arriving at the straight with reserves intact and enough to repel any finishing effort; the soft ground further saps the energy of hold-up horses asked to close a gap they never truly threatened.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Sweep Past
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just quick enough to stretch the field and one of the prominent-to-midfield horses lands a telling blow from a close-up position.
scenarios.body: Bay Of Myths or Kisiyra travels within a length or two of High Storm, saves energy in the slipstream, and produces a decisive move two furlongs out as the leader begins to tie up on the soft surface; What's The Plan, racing prominently in a hold-up role, is also well-placed to capitalise if the gallop suits ground-grinding stayers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Storms Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the hold-up horses manage to close meaningful ground in the final two furlongs despite their compromised starting positions.
scenarios.body: Wardlaw, a proven stayer with a win over 12f on good ground and consistent placed form at this trip, is the most likely beneficiary if the race falls apart for the leaders late; Mr Bollinger has winning form over 12f and could pick up pieces, though both are operating further back than ideal given the field's pace configuration.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Collapses, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If High Storm goes too fast for the conditions, blows up turning in, and leaves the door open for a horse making late headway from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Acklam has soft-ground form and has won at 13f, making her the natural beneficiary of a complete pace collapse, though her recent form figures of 9-5714 give little confidence; Knightsail's limited soft-ground profile makes this an unlikely vehicle for that horse specifically, but the scenario remains possible if conditions bite harder than the going report suggests.

watchPoints.text: High Storm's 99-day absence is a significant risk factor — if Burke's runner shows any signs of race-rustiness in the first half-mile or hangs under pressure, the controlled pace scenario unravels entirely and Bay Of Myths is best placed to pounce.

Wardlaw, Knightsail, and Mr Bollinger are all genuine closers competing in a race with a compressed rear-of-field — watch the early stages to see whether any of them manage to secure a position closer to the pace than expected, as that would materially change their winning chances.

What's The Plan steps into soft ground and 1m4f for the first time simultaneously; if Harry Davies moves forward to track the pace rather than ride a true hold-up race, the horse could be a sleeper from a prominent position given the consistent placed form.

Bay Of Myths is lightly raced at 1m4f for the first time and the yard is cold (0/13 last 14 days) — monitor market moves at the off, as significant support would suggest connections have strong confidence in the stamina.

The going report consistently lists this race as Good to Soft rather than Soft — if the ground is riding on the better end of that description, the advantage for the front-runner diminishes and the closers' chance of generating late momentum increases proportionally.

races.name: Thirsk Racecourse Ideal Conference & Events Venue Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Kosometsuke
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a Goodwood win 81 days ago over course-similar 7f in good ground; hold-up style means he needs something to happen up front but soft going suits his profile and Connor Beasley's patient hands will be critical if this pace is modest.|

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partnering a regular O'Meara runner who ran 2nd just 7 days ago over 8f in soft — the freshest form in the field and proven in this going; races hold-up but has shown ability to sit closer when pace is modest, making him one to watch for a prominent move into the straight.|

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Roger Fell runner whose recent form reads as a solid handicapper on good ground but has not produced a placed effort in his last five starts; the form figures in similar going are modest (2 from 15 attempts, no wins) and his hold-up style with no soft-ground win on record is a concern in this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Mythical Phoenix
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's six-year-old wants to race prominently and with only Good Karma likely ahead of her, she is well-placed to press the leader from the outset; form figures on soft are acceptable (3 from 15, 0 wins) but the recent string of 8s over 6f suggests this step to 7f could help, and David Allan is an astute Thirsk jockey.|

runners_data.name: Frankies Dream
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's four-year-old is a natural hold-up horse who has been shuffled into a midfield slot on the map through redistribution — her true place is at the rear, and in a race where the pace is modest, she will face a stern test launching a winning challenge from that position; soft-going record is thin (1 from 15).|

runners_data.name: Native Instinct
runners_data.note: Won over 7f in good ground and has course-distance form to point to; although genuinely a hold-up horse by inclination, Harry Davies may find a position closer to the pace given how many rivals are similarly inclined, and the soft-ground record (5 from 14, 1 win) is acceptable if not outstanding.|

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — note this in final selections; if they do run, this six-year-old has a tongue strap and is a true hold-up type, with soft-ground experience (4 from 15, 1 win) but overall form this season has been disappointing (form 389637).|

runners_data.name: Intrusively
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's mare has been running consistently in the placed positions over longer trips on good or standard; she is naturally suited further than 7f and, being a genuine hold-up operator forced into midfield by the field dynamics, the combination of a modest pace and potentially insufficient trip makes this assignment tough.|

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old boasts wins at 7f and an apprentice claiming allowance through Lauren Young, which is notable; however, five recent starts in similar going have yielded no placed effort, and as another true hold-up type sitting further forward than ideal, the style-fit concern is real despite the attractive weight.|

runners_data.name: Good Karma
runners_data.note: The key player: John David Riches's six-year-old is the lone confirmed front runner, and Ethan Tindall (5lb claimer) gets on well enough as a junior rider; dropping to OR 61 means rivals are all significantly better-rated, but if allowed to ping clear unchallenged on soft ground — as the shape suggests — the low weight and soft-ground experience (1 from 15, 1 win) could see him stay honest for much longer than his rating implies.|

races.paceDynamic: Good Karma is the lone confirmed front runner in this 10-runner field and, dropping significantly in class off OR 61, will be allowed to bowl along unchallenged on the Thirsk straight seven, setting a controlled, honest gallop on ground that will be riding good to soft at best. With no pressing rival to force the pace, the fractions are likely to be measured rather than truly searching, which historically on this flat track favours horses who can race prominently and quicken from the front half of the field. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can secure their natural position — Frankies Dream, Wreck It Ryley, Native Instinct, Native Honey and Intrusively are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and the only runners realistically able to press Good Karma into a prominent position are Mythical Phoenix and, to a lesser extent, Misunderstood. A modest, uncontested gallop on soft-ish ground at Thirsk over seven furlongs delivers its clearest verdict to prominent-tracking types who can sit just behind the leader, travel into the race and use the ground energy late — genuine closers who need a truly-run race are unlikely to get the strong pace they require to produce a devastating late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates Soft
scenarios.trigger: If Good Karma controls the race unchallenged at a comfortable gallop, draining the finishing speed of those coming from behind.
scenarios.body: Good Karma sets a gentle tempo that suits those tracking within two to three lengths, with the soft ground ensuring any big closer's move stalls in the straight; the race is effectively run as a procession that rewards positional racing rather than late bursts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overpowers
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker — particularly Mythical Phoenix or Misunderstood — travels sweetly into the straight and runs down Good Karma in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Good Karma's significant class and rating disadvantage leaves it vulnerable to a runner who simply sits in its slipstream and pounces; the soft ground rewards a horse with a high cruising speed and the ability to sustain its effort rather than produce a sudden sprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and creates a late opening for a hold-up horse that has found a clear run sooner than expected.
scenarios.body: A compressed, slowly-run race occasionally bunches the field and allows a well-handicapped closer to pick up ground in the final furlong, but with so many true hold-up types forced to race off a modest pace from midfield, the winning move is unlikely to materialise cleanly or early enough.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Winner Comes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so moderate that the whole field turns for home in a heap and the race becomes a sprint in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An extreme bunching scenario theoretically opens the door for any horse with an instant turn of foot, but on soft ground and over seven furlongs with so many horses genuinely out of their preferred role, the probability of a clean, decisive late swoop from deep is very low.

watchPoints.text: Good Karma (Ethan Tindall) — the only confirmed front runner; if he builds an early lead of more than three lengths unchallenged, the race could be over before the hold-up horses even get started.|

Mythical Phoenix (David Allan) — watch the start carefully; if she misses the break or fails to press Good Karma in the first two furlongs, the tactical advantage of her prominent style is lost and the race shape shifts entirely.|

Misunderstood (Jason Hart) — only seven days since his last run, which could mean he is at peak fitness or slightly fatigued; watch whether Hart positions him prominently or reverts to hold-up tactics, as it will tell you immediately what camp O'Meara is in with this horse.|

Wreck It Ryley is currently listed as a non-runner — connections and raceday declarations should be confirmed before forming a view on the final field size and pace shape, as removal of any runner alters the redistribution dynamic minimally but clarifies betting markets.|

The soft going declared for the 5:00 slot is notably softer than the good-to-soft reported for earlier races — if conditions deteriorate further through the afternoon, horses with proven soft-ground form (Misunderstood, Native Instinct) gain an additional edge over rivals with only good-ground credentials.|

races.name: Thirsk Racecourse Ideal Conference & Events Venue Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Stanley Spencer
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, racing off 81 with 14 days between runs; his sim-going record on soft reads just 1 win from 15 attempts, which casts genuine doubt on whether he can sustain his front-running role when the ground turns testing, though his most recent placed effort over 6f on soft offers mild encouragement.

runners_data.name: Obelix
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground and has form figures that include a recent fourth on good, but his five-race history shows a ⚠ fade tendency in the finish and all his best efforts have come on a sounder surface; this is his first start on soft and that transition is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Capital Guarantee
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's team are in strong form (7/50 over 14 days) and Billy Garritty rides a prominent type well-placed to track the pace throughout; only 2 wins from 15 on similar going is a caution, but his style fits this race shape better than most here.

runners_data.name: Midnight Strike
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's four-year-old has a win and two places from 8 runs on good-to-soft or softer, giving her the most relevant sim-going profile among the hold-up horses; racing over 7f after recent efforts at longer trips, and the step back in trip could sharpen her finish if the pace has been honest enough.

runners_data.name: Mr King
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground and carries headgear (h) that has coincided with his best efforts, but his finish-fade flag and a sim-going record of just 3 from 15 without a win on this type of ground suggest he could struggle when the soft turf blunts his late run.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins over 7f on good ground mark this horse as a genuine performer at this distance, but his true style is hold-up and he arrives here with almost no soft-ground form (1 from 15), meaning he is doubly compromised — racing out of his natural rear position and facing a surface that has not suited him historically.

runners_data.name: Packetofbiscuits
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose best recent form includes a second over 7f on standard Tapeta, but his turf soft-ground exposure is negligible (1 from 15); racing off a reduced OR of 72 with a claimer aboard, he will need a particularly well-run race to overcome both positional and going uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's seven-year-old switches from his habitual 6f trips to 7f here, which is the primary query given his form is built entirely around the shorter distance on good ground; if the extra furlong does not find him out, his prominent style would allow him to sit in a perfect stalking position behind Stanley Spencer.

runners_data.name: Nyman
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old has placed form at 7-8f on good ground and the trainer is 2/13 over the last 14 days, but his natural running style is genuine hold-up and the redistribution to midfield means he is unlikely to see out the race from his optimal position; on soft, his form reads 1 win from 15 with two places, offering a slim but real each-way thread if the pace falls right.

races.paceDynamic: Stanley Spencer is the lone confirmed front runner and, with only Fiscal Policy and Capital Guarantee as natural prominent types, he can expect to set a controlled, uncontested gallop from the front on soft ground over seven furlongs. That sustainable tempo — neither dawdling nor scorching — will reward horses who can track close to the pace and quicken in the straight rather than those who need a true end-to-end test to finish past beaten rivals. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Imperial Guard, Packetofbiscuits, and Nyman are genuine closers redistributed into midfield slots because they cannot all drop to the back of a nine-runner field, which means their true finishing kicks may be compromised by position. This shape — a lone leader setting a soft but honest clip on genuinely soft ground — primarily favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can travel smoothly in his slipstream and pounce when he tires in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Stanley Spencer leads at a comfortable clip and the soft ground gradually saps his stamina, allowing a close tracker to collar him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Stanley Spencer sets a measured tempo that suits those racing in his wake, and the soft surface ensures that even a controlled pace is energy-sapping enough to crack his resistance late; Capital Guarantee or Fiscal Policy, racing just off his shoulder, are ideally positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough on soft ground to string out the field and allow the truest hold-up horses to pick off tired rivals in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Soft going can legitimise a late run if the early sections are truly gruelling, giving Midnight Strike or Obelix — who have each won at this distance — the room to finish past fading competitors; however, several horses labelled as closers here are not truly racing from their natural position, which materially reduces the collective chance of this shape delivering.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves too genteel for the closers to overcome and Stanley Spencer is never seriously pressured throughout.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian gallop on soft ground can paradoxically suit a front runner who settles and conserves energy, and with no horse equipped or willing to press Stanley Spencer hard, he could simply idle into the straight and find enough to hold on; his sim-going record is modest but his form shows a recent placed effort at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up types do manage to find a clear run from midfield and the pace collapses in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Imperial Guard has a strong recent sequence of wins at seven furlongs on good ground and possesses proven finishing speed if the race somehow falls right, while Nyman has placed form in similar conditions; both would need luck in running and an untypically punishing pace to fully unlock their natural style from a compromised starting position.

watchPoints.text: Stanley Spencer's soft-ground record (1 win from 15 outings in similar conditions) is a critical flag — if he weakens sharply entering the straight, the entire race shape inverts and prominent holders Capital Guarantee and Fiscal Policy become the immediate beneficiaries.

Imperial Guard, Packetofbiscuits, and Nyman are all genuine hold-up horses mapped into midfield slots — watch for traffic congestion in the straight if they all attempt to come with runs simultaneously, which could block each other and benefit the front pair.

Obelix has a documented fade tendency and no soft-ground form on record; if he tracks the pace prominently in the early stages, his finish could collapse completely on this testing surface, creating a false picture of the race's tempo.

Fiscal Policy steps up to 7f for the first time from a career built over 6f — watch his behaviour in the early furlongs to assess whether he settles or burns petrol trying to match Stanley Spencer's stride, which would compromise his chance significantly.
Capital Guarantee's trainer David O'Meara is striking at 14% over the last 14 days (7/50), a meaningful live-yard flag in a race where the horse's prominent style fits the expected shape well.
